## 開篇固定收益論點

8月17日美國固定收益市場收盤凸顯一項分化：Fed 近期政策路徑的威脅減輕，長天期債券的代價卻愈來愈高。美國2年期公債殖利率上升2個基點至4.19%，5年期上升2個基點至4.38%，10年期上升4個基點至4.72%，30年期上升6個基點至5.31%，創2007年以來最高。2s10s殖利率曲線走陡2個基點至53個基點，2s30s擴大4個基點至112個基點。若拉長至1個月，差距更為明顯：2年期僅上升1個基點，10年期與30年期則分別上升17個與25個基點。市場已不再將 Fed 下次決策視為約束存續期間部位的主要因素。

兩股力量強化了這項判斷。美國與伊朗6月簽署的備忘錄到期，雙方未能達成持久和平協議，總統唐納．川普也表示無意延長，油價因而再度帶回通膨風險。WTI上漲3.05%至$84.91，Brent上漲2.94%至$91.12。然而，10年期損益兩平通膨率僅上升1個基點至2.28%，10年期實質殖利率則上升3個基點至2.44%。黎巴嫩戰事再起、荷姆茲海峽周邊運輸持續受阻，使能源因素不容忽視，但指標公債大部分跌勢仍來自實質折現率。聯邦年度赤字接近$2兆、邊際美債買方對價格異常敏感，再加上 AI 帶動的企業借款週期創紀錄，三者正在競逐同一批長期資本。

政策端無法以偏鷹立場解釋這波走勢。就業、通膨與零售銷售數據轉弱後，交易員將下次 Fed 升息1碼的預期時點，由一週前的12月推遲至1月。美元指數下跌0.13%至99.54，黃金期貨上漲2.25%至$4,479.10。這些走勢反映 Fed 眼前的政策壓力下降，並不代表市場認定通膨與制度風險已經消失。S&P 500下跌0.52%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.17%，半導體指數卻上漲1.64%。股市一方面保留對 AI 盈餘週期的信心，另一方面也開始反映長端殖利率墊高的融資門檻。

信用市場仍然暢通，但存續期間與發行人品質拉開報酬差距。8月美國投資級債發行量達到創紀錄的$1,452億，Blackstone Private Credit Fund與Blue Owl Technology Finance週一的發行規模均高於原定目標。與此同時，長存續期間總報酬走弱：LQD下跌0.40%，HYG與JNK跌幅約0.13%，美國政府20年以上債券指數下跌0.77%。這些價格不足以證明現金債利差已經變動，卻顯示當日損失集中於存續期間，並非低品質信用資產遭到全面撤資。個別壓力事件是例外，其中以Sammons Financial債券及數起重整案最突出；在這些案例中，擔保品、發起人支持與流動性仍是關鍵。

國際市場也顯示，美國走勢不能孤立看待。日本第2季成長不如預期，但日圓防衛、輸入型通膨與欠缺財源的財政承諾，使日本央行9月升息仍有可能，10年期殖利率因而升至2.93%，創1996年以來最高。印度則出現不同的政策衝擊：央行提前終止外幣存款專案，市場因而下修盧比流動性預期，5年期殖利率一度上升9個基點。相較之下，希臘因預算盈餘降低未來融資需求，計畫提前償還約EUR130億債務。全球存續期間資產並非受到單一成長動能驅動；各地財政選擇、匯率限制與供給決策，正形成日益分歧的市場出清價格。

## 財政存續期間壓力遇上 AI 融資週期

週一美債殖利率曲線完全逆轉了7月通膨與消費數據轉弱後，由前端領漲的債市反彈。30年期殖利率來到5.31%，較前一週$250億標售的得標殖利率5.216%高出10個基點。10年期收在4.72%，也高於先前$420億標售的4.683%截止殖利率。先前標售已證明，歷史高檔殖利率足以吸引需求。如今的新訊息是：油價再度上漲、企業長天期債券持續湧入後，即使標售承接尚稱充足，也未能為殖利率建立持久上限。

殖利率拆解結果削弱了單以油價解釋跌勢的說法。10年期名目殖利率上升4個基點，其中實質殖利率上升3個基點，損益兩平通膨率上升1個基點。30年期實質殖利率上升6個基點至3.06%，與長債名目殖利率變化一致，2年期名目殖利率則僅上升2個基點。因此，即使市場預期 Fed 路徑轉趨溫和，殖利率曲線仍要求遠期現金流提供更高的實質補償。能源價格上漲可能推高最終通膨水準，並使央行更難保持耐心，但各期限的走勢指向更廣泛的資本配置問題。

聯邦借款仍是這項負擔的最大來源。政府每年赤字接近$2兆，債務管理更倚重短期發行，同時維持10年期與30年期標售規模不變。Barclays估計，今年由民間投資人承接的美國中長期公債淨供給約$1.2兆，較2025年減少$4,400億。供給減少仍未紓解市場壓力，原因是企業債淨供給預計增加$4,740億，其中大部分來自科技公司。一個管道減少的存續期間供給由另一個管道補上，整體儲蓄需求並未下降。

AI融資規模如今已足以影響美債相對價值，不再只影響個別企業債利差。投資級公司今年已發行近$1.5兆債券，較去年同期增加36%。大型科技公司的借款約$2,000億，相當於民間投資人承接之美國中長期公債淨發行量的約25%，也是2025年占比的5倍。長天期債券在發行日程中的比重也更高：10年以上債券約占2026年投資級發行量20%，高於2025年的13%。因此新增的$1,900億長天期企業債，接近30年期美債全年供給$2,760億的70%。

傳導機制十分直接。高評等科技債的殖利率高於存續期間相近的政府債，促使部分核心債券基金減持美債，為企業債配置籌措資金。Alphabet近期30年期債券殖利率接近6.4%，較可比美債高約115個基點；一檔與Meta相關的資料中心債券殖利率超過7.5%。Morningstar資料顯示，美國投資級債券基金將企業債平均配置提高至3年高點30%，同時降低美債持有部位。Bank of America經濟學家估計，企業債與房貸抵押證券發行增加，使今年10年期殖利率上升約30個基點。這項估計仍有不確定性，但方向與供給結構及當日由實質殖利率帶動的曲線走陡一致。

週一增加的是實際發行規模，而非同一主題的另一種說法。8月投資級債發行量達$1,452億，超過2020年寫下的先前單月紀錄$1,360億。今年迄今供給為$1.46兆，較該創紀錄年度同期高8.5%。Alphabet本月在美國發行$250億債券，規模居冠，也是2026年第8筆至少達此規模的交易，且全數由科技業借款人發行。JPMorgan將科技、媒體與電信業全年美元債發行預測上調約20%至$5,400億。美國勞動節假期後發行通常加速，意味資產負債表承接能力面臨的競爭尚未到達明確的季節性終點。

同一週期也正跨越不同幣別。Alphabet開始行銷首次澳幣債券交易，共分4種期限，包括一檔20年期券，目標規模約A$50億，或$36億。該公司先前已發行美元、瑞士法郎、英鎊、歐元、加幣與日圓債券，且上月將2026年資本支出預測調高至最高$2,050億。澳洲境外借款人發行速度創紀錄，加上當地科技業曝險有限，可能有助交易執行。然而，從全球存續期間角度來看，這筆交易顯示超大規模雲端業者正動用多個國內儲蓄池，而非將融資壓力侷限於美國信用市場。

實體原油流向是近期最主要的限制條件。儘管船隻遭到攻擊，秘密轉運仍讓中東產油國將大量原油輸往阿曼灣，使價格漲幅低於供應完全中斷的情境。這套緩和機制與美國及伊朗協議到期、黎巴嫩戰事再起，以及川普稱海上封鎖正在施壓、但未提出解決時程等因素並存。週一損益兩平通膨率僅小幅上升，顯示市場並未將油價單日上漲3%完全外推至長期通膨。若替代運輸失效，或荷姆茲海峽交通遭遇更廣泛干擾，存續期間資產跌勢將有更大部分由實質殖利率轉向通膨補償，並使長端重新連結 Fed 路徑。

## 日圓防衛壓過疲弱需求

日本最清楚地呈現央行即使面對內需疲弱，仍受通膨與匯率掣肘的情境。第2季實質GDP年化成長1.1%，低於市場共識2%，也慢於第1季修正後的1.9%。經濟雖連續第3季擴張，組成卻不理想：民間消費持平，不如預期的成長0.4%；資本投資在非年化基礎下降1.2%，前季數據修正為下降1%，也不如原先預估的成長0.5%。這份數據削弱了強勁內需要求央行立即收緊政策的論點。

債市卻更加重視匯率、通膨與財政限制。日本10年期殖利率一度上升5.5個基點至2.93%，創1996年以來最高。20年期殖利率上升6.5個基點至3.815%，30年期上升6個基點至4.07%，接近5月創下的紀錄。隔夜交換市場顯示，9月18日升息機率約為80%。疲弱的GDP細項或許降低連續升息的理由，卻未能動搖近期升息1次的預期。

日圓可以解釋升息預期為何如此穩固。日圓交易價接近159兌1美元，遠弱於10年平均126.09，且只從7月觸及的40年低點163.99部分回升。美國與日本在該月底聯手干預，減緩了日圓跌勢，卻未消除利差。首相高市早苗的政府支持日本央行近期升息，時間可能落在9月或10月；日本央行總裁植田和男在7月將政策利率維持於1%後，也已強調通膨上行風險。如今，升息與其被描述為因應強勁產出，不如視為匯率穩定策略的一環。

前財務官中尾武彥提出更積極的主張。他表示，日本央行應在每次會議升息，並將基準利率提高至2%以上；若通膨約為2%，2.25%或2.5%也不算異常。他將日圓極度疲弱直接歸因於利差，並指出日本擁有$1.2兆外匯存底，仍有干預能力。中尾並非現任政策制定者，但其言論擴大了公開討論中的緊縮情境，從預期升息1次延伸至可能更快的升息序列。

即使需求轉弱，國內通膨仍讓這項立場站得住腳。7月企業物價年增7.2%，企業將燃料與原物料成本上升轉嫁給消費者的壓力加大。荷姆茲海峽實際上仍處於封閉狀態，日本被迫分散石油供應來源；美國占6月進口量近三分之一，2月時僅占7%。穩健的年度薪資成長與公用事業補貼日後或能支撐消費，卻無法消除當前的分配問題：薪資與資產增值較少的家庭，在政府增加紓困措施之際仍須承受更高生活成本。

財政政策進一步加重長端風險。高市政府已限制公用事業費率，並計畫自4月起將食品消費稅降至1%，為期2年，但尚未說明財源。家庭支持措施可緩衝輸入型通膨對成長的傷害，欠缺財源的紓困卻會加重規模已超過經濟產值2倍的公共債務負擔。這套政策不利長天期JGB：貨幣緊縮提高折現率，財政補償則可能在民間需求疲弱時維持供給與通膨壓力。

日本的結果是全球債券分散效果不再同步的縮影。32個交換市場中，三分之二已定價升息，未來1年7個主要市場合計隱含約400個基點的緊縮幅度。南韓定價的升息幅度超過100個基點，居各國之首；其政府債以本幣計價今年已下跌近9%，日本債券則下跌約4%。法國10年期殖利率近期觸及2009年以來最高，德國與義大利殖利率今年均上升逾30個基點。各國政策情境並不相同，但合併來看，即使 Fed 升息預期轉弱，外國長天期主權債也未必上漲。

中國是重要的反例。7月工業生產年增率放緩至4.5%，零售銷售年增率降至0.6%，前7個月固定資產投資下降6.7%，城鎮失業率升至5.2%。電子設備產量成長逾19%，顯示 AI 相關生產與整體經濟明顯分化。8月17日中國政策性銀行債指數上漲0.08%，走勢與美國及其他已開發市場長天期債券的跌勢相反。這項分歧證實各地成長與政策限制仍然重要，但中國無法提供足夠的全球需求緩衝，抵銷能源進口經濟體的緊縮壓力。

## 流動性決策重塑主權債殖利率曲線

印度央行將海外居民的美元存款專案提前1個月至8月底關閉，在殖利率曲線前端造成局部衝擊。這項決策令交易員意外，因為印度央行總裁Sanjay Malhotra在8月5日政策會議上曾排除提前結束。5年期政府債殖利率一度上升9個基點至6.44%，10年期則上升4個基點至6.80%。各期限走勢反映流動性機制：外幣存款減少，意味未來可支撐短天期債券的盧比流動性下降。

該專案先前已吸引逾$500億資金，並協助外匯存底在3週內增加逾$300億至$7,070億。Citigroup將總流入預測下調至$700億，較原先估計少$100億，並預期近期盧比升值幅度將受限於約95兌1美元。盧比週一下跌0.2%至95.58。RBI似乎認為，增加外匯存底與流動性的效益，已不足以抵銷3至5年期外幣借款形成的未來負債，以及央行承擔的遠期溢價成本。

提前關閉並未終止所有融資管道。國營企業與銀行的其他專案仍開放至12月，境外借款優惠交換提供固定年利率1.5%，平均期限至少3年。印度金融機構今年已發行創紀錄的$80億美元債，超過2019年全年舊紀錄$79.2億。ICICI Bank週一正在行銷另一筆交易，Kotak Mahindra Bank與Yes Bank也已聘請顧問，準備可能的指標型發行。銀行可能在存款帶來的動能消退前加快發債，之後隨一般避險成本再度使境外借款較不划算而放慢。

印度的發展顯示，央行資產負債表決策可以重新分配融資壓力，而非將其消除。存款窗口原本支撐外匯存底、盧比與國內流動性；提前終止後，本地殖利率上升，預期匯率效益下降。仍開放的借款專案鼓勵銀行發行美元債，將部分需求移往全球信用市場。近期銀行債因訂單強勁，最終定價利差得以較初始指引收窄，顯示管道仍正常運作。邊際成本已從RBI未來的遠期曝險，轉移至國內債券持有人與境外投資人。

希臘則釋出相反的主權債訊號，利用財政表現優於預期提前償債。政府計畫於2026年提前償還約EUR130億，包括約EUR25億歐洲金融穩定機制貸款，以及一檔2027年到期、規模EUR22億的債券。政府也預計在12月31日前將流通國庫券減少EUR12億。計畫尚未定案，但希臘6月已償還EUR69億紓困貸款，目標是在年底前使其債務存量低於義大利。

改善來自預算盈餘與流動性，而非僅靠換券延長期限。希臘預期基本盈餘將再度超越目標，今年債務占GDP比率將由原估的138.2%降至137%，年底現金準備將超過EUR300億。提前償還降低未來融資需求，因此即使償還2027年到期債券，2027年融資策略仍可與今年相近。希臘10年期殖利率已低於義大利、法國與英國，顯示可信的供給縮減可以抵銷全球期限補償上升。

新興市場抗通膨債券呈現另一種分化。規模$8,860億的市場在2026年至週五止報酬率達11.1%，相較之下，整體本幣債報酬率為1.6%，全球綜合債券指標則下跌0.2%。貨幣升值放大了報酬，拉丁美洲尤其明顯；哥倫比亞披索、巴西里爾與墨西哥披索是今年表現最強的3種新興市場貨幣。然而，隨巴西隱含通膨轉貴、名目長端利率升至15%左右，交易選擇性日益提高。波蘭看來相對便宜，部分原因是發行量較大，卻缺少巴西既有的退休基金自然需求；智利與哥倫比亞則提供較均衡的抗通膨債評價。

這種分化之所以重要，是因為共同通膨衝擊正透過不同買方基礎與政策反應傳導。土耳其將年底通膨預測由26%上調至28%；阿根廷、印度、南非與羅馬尼亞近期通膨數據也高於預期，巴西與哥倫比亞通膨則持續僵固。聖嬰現象可能進一步推升拉丁美洲食品與電力價格壓力。抗通膨債仍是反映實際通膨與匯率強勢的有效工具，但先前報酬已無法取代針對各國供給、實質殖利率與央行可信度的個別評估。

## 信用管道暢通掩蓋更尖銳的損失分配

週一初級信用市場顯示，資金充沛與更嚴格的差別定價可以並存。Blackstone Private Credit Fund原先目標約$5億，最終發行$7.5億5年期債券，高峰訂單約$20億。Blue Owl Technology Finance在6月交易基礎上增發$4億，為最低目標的2倍，需求約$10.5億。Blue Owl新債以美債加250個基點定價，低於既有債券265個基點的溢價；Blackstone則以加205個基點定價，較初步討論收窄約25個基點。

這些結果值得注意，因為部分私人信貸工具的軟體業曝險與贖回限制，曾在今年稍早引發擔憂。第2季財報減輕部分疑慮，這些交易也證明發行人能以投資級條件進入市場。但前一週投資人見最終利差收窄後，平均撤回36%的初始訂單，顯示整體選擇性並未改變。即使訂單強勁，承銷過程仍須保留投資人要求的補償。

Project Odyssey清楚反映這種價格敏感度。Blackstone支持的QTS在需求超過$80億後，可能將與Microsoft相關的喬治亞州資料中心融資規模提高至$39億。5年期債券預計取得投資級評等，但6%後段的票息與折價發行價，將使殖利率落在7%初段至中段，與單B級債券相當。長期租約與Microsoft關係支撐交易結構，但投資人獲得的收益，仍是在補償並非直接留在超大規模雲端業者一般資產負債表上的專案、施工與集中度風險。QTS在4月曾為Microsoft運算能力籌資$46億，高峰需求達$125億；新債殖利率顯示，能夠反覆進入市場不等於融資成本低廉。

次級信用市場則發出更嚴重的治理訊號。Sammons Financial的2036年6月到期債券利差，由一週前的147個基點擴大至較指標約200個基點，創發行以來最弱。相關報導聚焦該保險公司與Guggenheim Partners之間的關係，包括申報文件將Sammons列為關係人，並承認相關誘因可能造成利益衝突。Hunterbrook Media揭露其投資關係企業放空這些債券；評估該報導動機時，這項資訊是重要的限制條件。Fitch在6月給予Sammons A-評等，理由包括資本極為雄厚，但風險資產曝險略高。

疑慮不只是一筆利差變動。Sammons曾是Guggenheim最大股東，而Guggenheim替這家保險公司管理數百億美元資產。美國檢察官與監管機構正在調查與Mark Walter有關的保險公司貸款，這些資金被導向其商業版圖的其他部分。Guggenheim一筆2031年11月到期的第一順位定期貸款，週一報價低於面額的80%，低於7月20日前後的面額水準。關係人曝險、交叉持股與債價下跌並存，使控制權與資產移轉風險的重要性，超過表面溫和的整體高評級發行日程。

巴西顯示，限制性利率與財政不確定性如何讓總體緊縮轉化為企業困境。央行活動指數6月下降0.64%，差於市場共識的下降0.5%，也是2025年5月以來最大跌幅。第2季經濟仍成長0.2%，年增2.35%，但第1季財政刺激退去後，利率敏感產業正失去動能。政策制定者8月連續第4次會議將Selic利率下調25個基點至14%，9月決策將取決於新公布的通膨與經濟活動數據。通膨仍高於3%目標，限制寬鬆速度。

財政部長Dario Durigan承認，投資人對強制性支出與公共債務軌跡的擔憂有其道理。巴西里爾前一週已連續5個交易日走弱；隨總統Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva擴大選舉領先優勢，截至8月12日，外資已從當地股市撤出逾135億里爾，或$26億。通膨預期至2028年仍高於目標。Durigan指出，財政政策是政府能控制、用以降低結構性高利率的主要工具，卻未支持修改退休金指數化機制或財政架構的支出規則。政府已承認問題，但尚未提出具體調整。

Casas Bahia反映其企業後果。這家零售商在2024年庭外重整未能恢復流動性後，進入法院監督的破產保護程序。公司列舉高利率、信用收緊、融資成本、消費疲弱與營運資金壓力等原因，並申報負債173億里爾。上半年淨營收為144億里爾，淨損則達112億里爾，較去年同期擴大18.4%。公司已關閉298家門市，並計畫在延長債務期限期間維持其餘業務營運。法律程序能保留營運，卻無法恢復盈餘能見度或債權人價值。

Braskem則是另一樁由期限推動的重整案。Petrobras正考慮延長付款期限、降低利率並增加石腦油供應；先前較嚴格的條件，已使其占Braskem原料供應的比重從最高70%降至約30%，迫使這家石化公司增加銀行借款。改善商業條件可降低營運資金借款與槓桿。然而，目前尚未決定，也沒有時程；Braskem必須在8月24日前取得至少三分之一債務持有人的支持，才能完成庭外解決方案並避免司法重整。

擬議支援也凸顯利害關係人衝突。Braskem股份曾為210億里爾未償銀行貸款提供擔保，這些貸款最終出售給IG4 Capital管理的基金，後者目前共同掌握控制權。包括Elliott Investment Management與Contrarian Capital在內的債券持有人，希望Petrobras提供股本、營運資金或次順位債務。Petrobras拒絕注資，因為提高持股可能迫使其將Braskem債務併入自身資產負債表。商業讓步或能改善流動性，卻無法解決國營股東、銀行與債券持有人之間如何分攤損失與新資本。

Modernland Realty顯示亞洲也出現類似的價值移轉。這家印尼開發商提議將$2.745億美元債到期日由2027年4月延至2028年6月，最終再交換為永續證券，並以移轉至債權人控制載體的資產提供支持。持有人每$1,000本金將先收到$50，按3%利率累積實物支付利息，未支付利息則計入本金。部分現有擔保品將解除，以擔保一筆新的$3,400萬融資。8月24日投票期限使這套方案成為當前決策重點：延長到期日與取得新流動性的代價，是現金利息延後、擔保條件改變及回收期拉長。

## 前瞻市場意涵

8月19日公布的7月FOMC會議紀要，以及主席Kevin Warsh本月稍晚在Jackson Hole的談話，需要說明政策制定者如何衡量近期就業、通膨與零售銷售數據連續轉弱。7月決策以9比3維持利率不變，目前市場已將下次升息時點推至1月。若措辭顯示維持利率不變的決定比票數呈現得更接近，或強調核心商品中仍有逾55%持續漲價，2年期殖利率可能跟隨長端上升。若政策解讀偏向耐心，顯示央行緊縮前仍需觀察數個數據點，陡峭的殖利率曲線將得以維持，財政供給、AI發債與實質殖利率也將繼續主導存續期間資產。

$160億20年期美債標售，是下一個直接檢驗跌勢最重期限區段出清價格的事件。30年期殖利率收在5.31%，當日上升6個基點；20年以上現貨交易量較前一交易日增加15.1%，以原始面額計達$1,344億。若標售結果接近當時發行殖利率，且次級市場交易穩定，將顯示最新讓利後仍有需求。若出現明顯標售尾差，或標售後曲線再度走陡，則表示8月創紀錄的企業債供給與全球主權債殖利率上升，仍蓋過 Fed 路徑轉鴿帶來的緩解。

能源管道需要實體層面的解決，而非另一則外交標題。秘密原油轉運持續、船隻恢復通行，以及運費或保險成本下降，將減輕推升Brent至$91.12的壓力，並使最近美債跌勢繼續集中於實質殖利率。若替代流向失效、攻擊再起，或伊朗港口周邊執法收緊，衝擊將擴散至通膨補償與政策定價。判別關鍵在於損益兩平通膨率與2年期殖利率是否隨油價一同上升，或殖利率曲線是否繼續走陡，且調整大多集中於長端實質利率。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 17 U.S. fixed-income close sharpened the split between a less threatening near-term Federal Reserve path and an increasingly expensive long-duration market. The 2-year Treasury yield rose 2 basis points to 4.19%, the 5-year added 2 basis points to 4.38%, the 10-year increased 4 basis points to 4.72%, and the 30-year climbed 6 basis points to 5.31%, its highest level since 2007. The 2s10s curve steepened 2 basis points to 53 and 2s30s widened 4 basis points to 112. Over 1 month, the contrast is larger: the 2-year is only 1 basis point higher, against increases of 17 basis points at 10 years and 25 basis points at 30 years. The market is no longer treating the Fed's next decision as the principal constraint on duration.

Two forces reinforced that conclusion. Oil reintroduced inflation risk as the June U.S.-Iran memorandum expired without a durable peace agreement and President Donald Trump said he was not interested in extending it. WTI rose 3.05% to $84.91 and Brent gained 2.94% to $91.12. Yet the 10-year breakeven increased only 1 basis point to 2.28%, compared with a 3-basis-point rise in the 10-year real yield to 2.44%. Energy mattered, particularly after renewed fighting in Lebanon and continuing disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, but most of the benchmark selloff came through the real discount rate. Nearly $2 trillion annual federal deficits, an unusually price-sensitive marginal Treasury buyer and a record corporate borrowing cycle tied to artificial intelligence are competing for the same long-term capital.

The policy sector did not provide a hawkish explanation for the move. Following softer employment, inflation and retail-sales data, traders pushed the expected timing of the next quarter-point Fed increase to January from December a week earlier. The dollar index fell 0.13% to 99.54, and gold futures rose 2.25% to $4,479.10. Those moves fit a reduction in immediate Fed pressure, not a conviction that inflation and institutional risk have disappeared. The S&P 500 lost 0.52% and the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.17%, even as the semiconductor index gained 1.64%. Equity performance retained confidence in the AI earnings cycle while beginning to register the higher financing hurdle imposed by long yields.

Credit remained open, but duration and issuer quality separated outcomes. August U.S. investment-grade issuance reached a record $145.2 billion, and Blackstone Private Credit Fund and Blue Owl Technology Finance both increased Monday's offerings above their initial targets. At the same time, long-duration total returns weakened: LQD fell 0.40%, compared with declines of about 0.13% in HYG and JNK, and a U.S. government 20-plus-year bond index lost 0.77%. These prices do not establish a cash-spread move, but they show that the session's damage was concentrated in duration rather than a broad withdrawal from lower-quality credit. The exception was idiosyncratic stress, led by Sammons Financial bonds and several restructuring situations where collateral, sponsor support and liquidity remain decisive.

The international evidence argues against viewing the U.S. move in isolation. Japan's 10-year yield reached 2.93%, the highest since 1996, even after second-quarter growth disappointed, because yen defense, imported inflation and an unfunded fiscal promise kept a September Bank of Japan increase in play. India produced a different policy shock by ending a special foreign-currency deposit facility early, reducing expected rupee liquidity and sending its 5-year yield as much as 9 basis points higher. Greece, by contrast, plans about EUR13 billion of early debt repayment as budget surpluses reduce future financing needs. Global duration is not moving under one growth impulse; local fiscal choices, currency constraints and supply decisions are setting increasingly different clearing prices.

## Fiscal Duration Meets the AI Funding Cycle

Monday's Treasury curve completed a reversal of the front-end-led relief that followed July's softer inflation and consumption data. The 30-year yield at 5.31% stood 10 basis points above the 5.216% yield awarded at the prior week's $25 billion auction. The 10-year closed at 4.72%, above the 4.683% stop on the preceding $42 billion sale. Those auctions had already shown that demand was available at historically high yields. The new information is that adequate auction absorption did not establish a durable ceiling once oil rose again and corporate duration continued to arrive.

The decomposition limits the oil-only explanation. A 10-year nominal increase of 4 basis points was divided between a 3-basis-point rise in the real yield and a 1-basis-point increase in breakeven inflation. The 30-year real yield rose 6 basis points to 3.06%, matching the nominal long-bond change, while the 2-year nominal yield moved only 2 basis points. The curve therefore demanded more real compensation for distant cash flows even as the expected Fed path became less aggressive. A higher energy price can raise the inflation destination and complicate the central bank's patience, but the maturity pattern points to a broader capital-allocation problem.

Federal borrowing remains the largest source of that burden. The government is running deficits of nearly $2 trillion a year, and debt management has relied more heavily on short-term issuance while keeping 10- and 30-year auction sizes steady. Barclays estimated net Treasury note and bond supply to private investors at about $1.2 trillion this year, $440 billion less than in 2025. That reduction has not relieved the market because net corporate bond supply is expected to increase by $474 billion, much of it from technology companies. The duration removed from one channel has been replaced through another, without reducing the aggregate savings requirement.

AI financing is now large enough to affect Treasury relative value rather than merely individual corporate spreads. Investment-grade companies have issued nearly $1.5 trillion this year, 36% more than a year earlier. Borrowing by the largest technology companies is roughly $200 billion, equivalent to about 25% of Treasury's net note and bond issuance to private investors and five times the 2025 proportion. Long maturities also make up more of the calendar: debt beyond 10 years represents about 20% of 2026 investment-grade issuance, up from 13% in 2025. The resulting additional $190 billion of long-dated corporate bonds is nearly 70% of the $276 billion annual supply of 30-year Treasuries.

The mechanism is direct. Highly rated technology bonds offer more yield than governments with similar duration, inducing some core funds to fund allocations by reducing Treasury holdings. Alphabet's recent 30-year debt yielded nearly 6.4%, about 115 basis points over comparable Treasuries, and a Meta-linked data-center bond yielded more than 7.5%. Morningstar data show investment-grade U.S. bond funds increased average corporate allocations to a three-year high of 30% while reducing Treasury holdings. Bank of America economists estimated that heavier corporate and mortgage-backed issuance added about 30 basis points to the 10-year yield this year. The estimate is uncertain, but the direction is consistent with both the supply composition and the session's real-yield-led steepening.

Monday added realized scale rather than a new version of the same theme. August investment-grade sales reached $145.2 billion, surpassing the previous monthly record of $136 billion set in 2020. Year-to-date supply stood at $1.46 trillion, 8.5% ahead of the comparable point in that record year. Alphabet's $25 billion U.S. sale led the month and was the eighth transaction of at least that size in 2026, all from technology borrowers. JPMorgan raised its forecast for annual technology, media and telecommunications dollar issuance by about 20% to $540 billion. The usual acceleration after the U.S. Labor Day holiday means the competition for balance sheet has not reached an obvious seasonal endpoint.

The same cycle is moving across currencies. Alphabet began marketing its debut Australian-dollar deal in four maturities, including a 20-year tranche, with a target of about A$5 billion, or $3.6 billion. The company had already issued in U.S. dollars, Swiss francs, sterling, euros, Canadian dollars and yen, and last month raised its 2026 capital-spending forecast to as much as $205 billion. Australia's record pace of offshore-borrower issuance and limited local technology exposure may support execution. From the global duration perspective, however, the transaction shows that hyperscalers are drawing on multiple domestic savings pools rather than confining their funding pressure to U.S. credit.

Physical oil flows are the principal near-term qualification. Covert transfers have allowed Middle Eastern producers to move substantial crude into the Gulf of Oman despite attacks on vessels, limiting the price increase relative to a complete interruption. That mitigating mechanism coexists with an expiring U.S.-Iran agreement, renewed Lebanon fighting and Trump's statement that the naval blockade is exerting pressure without a timeline for resolution. Monday's modest breakeven move suggests the market did not extrapolate the full 3% daily oil rise into long-run inflation. Failure of those alternative flows, or a broader disruption of Hormuz traffic, would shift more of the duration selloff from real yields into inflation compensation and reconnect the long end with the Fed path.

## Japan's Yen Defense Overrides Weak Demand

Japan delivered the clearest example of a central bank facing an inflation and currency constraint despite weak domestic demand. Second-quarter real GDP grew at a 1.1% annualized rate, below the 2% consensus and slower than a revised 1.9% in the first quarter. The economy still expanded for a third consecutive quarter, but the composition was poor: private consumption was flat against an expected 0.4% increase, and capital investment fell 1.2% on a non-annualized basis after a revised 1% decline, instead of the forecast 0.5% gain. The result weakened the argument that a strong domestic economy requires immediate restraint.

The bond market nevertheless priced the currency, inflation and fiscal constraints more heavily. Japan's 10-year yield rose as much as 5.5 basis points to 2.93%, its highest since 1996. The 20-year yield increased 6.5 basis points to 3.815%, and the 30-year climbed 6 basis points to 4.07%, close to the record reached in May. Overnight swaps assigned about an 80% probability to a September 18 increase. The weak GDP details may reduce the case for consecutive moves, but they did not dislodge expectations of one near-term hike.

The yen explains much of that resilience. It traded near 159 per dollar, considerably weaker than its 10-year average of 126.09 and only partly recovered from the four-decade low of 163.99 reached in July. Coordinated U.S.-Japan intervention at the end of that month slowed the decline without removing the rate differential. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government supports a near-term BOJ increase, likely in September or October, and Governor Kazuo Ueda had already highlighted upside inflation risks after holding the policy rate at 1% in July. A hike can now be presented less as a response to robust output than as part of a currency-stabilization strategy.

Takehiko Nakao, a former vice finance minister for international affairs, made the more aggressive version of that argument. He said the BOJ should raise rates at every meeting and take the benchmark above 2%, adding that 2.25% or 2.5% would not be unusual with inflation around 2%. He linked the yen's extreme weakness directly to the interest-rate gap and pointed to Japan's $1.2 trillion of foreign reserves as continued intervention capacity. Nakao is not a current policymaker, yet his comments broaden the public range of tightening outcomes from one expected hike toward a potentially faster sequence.

Domestic inflation keeps that position credible even as demand softens. Corporate-goods prices rose 7.2% year on year in July, increasing the pressure on businesses to pass higher fuel and material costs to customers. Japan has had to diversify oil supply while Hormuz remains effectively closed; the United States supplied almost one-third of June imports, compared with 7% in February. Solid annual wage gains and utility subsidies may support consumption later, but they do not erase the present distributional problem: households with fewer wage and asset gains are absorbing higher living costs while the government adds relief measures.

Fiscal policy reinforces the long-end risk. Takaichi has capped utility costs and plans to cut the food sales tax to 1% for two years from April, without yet clarifying how that measure will be financed. Support for households can cushion the growth damage from imported inflation, but unfunded relief adds to a public-debt burden already exceeding twice the size of the economy. The resulting policy mix is unfavorable for long JGBs: monetary tightening raises discount rates, and fiscal compensation can preserve supply and inflation pressure even when private demand is weak.

The Japanese outcome is part of a broader loss of synchronized bond diversification. Across 32 swap markets, two-thirds are priced for rate increases, with about 400 basis points of tightening embedded across seven major markets over the coming year. South Korea leads with more than 100 basis points priced, and its government bonds have lost nearly 9% this year in local-currency terms; Japanese bonds are down about 4%. France's 10-year yield recently reached its highest since 2009, and German and Italian yields have risen more than 30 basis points this year. These are not identical policy stories, but together they reduce the likelihood that foreign sovereign duration will rally simply because Fed expectations soften.

China supplies the important counterexample. July industrial production growth slowed to 4.5% year on year, retail-sales growth weakened to 0.6%, fixed-asset investment fell 6.7% over the first seven months, and the urban unemployment rate rose to 5.2%. Electronic-equipment output grew more than 19%, showing a sharp divide between AI-linked production and the broader economy. A China policy-bank bond index gained 0.08% on August 17, opposite the losses in U.S. and other developed-market duration. The divergence confirms that local growth and policy constraints still matter; it does not provide enough global demand relief to offset tightening in energy-importing economies.

## Liquidity Decisions Reshape Sovereign Curves

India's central bank created a localized front-end shock by closing its special dollar-deposit window for overseas residents at the end of August, one month earlier than scheduled. The decision surprised traders because Governor Sanjay Malhotra had ruled out an early end at the August 5 policy meeting. The 5-year government yield rose as much as 9 basis points to 6.44%, compared with a 4-basis-point increase in the 10-year to 6.80%. That maturity pattern followed the liquidity mechanism: fewer foreign-currency deposits mean less prospective rupee liquidity available to support shorter bonds.

The facility had already attracted more than $50 billion and helped increase foreign-exchange reserves by over $30 billion in three weeks to $707 billion. Citigroup reduced its forecast for total gross inflows to $70 billion, $10 billion below its earlier estimate, and expected recent rupee appreciation to be capped around 95 per dollar. The currency weakened 0.2% to 95.58 on Monday. The RBI appears to have judged that additional reserves and liquidity no longer justified the future liability from three- to five-year foreign borrowing and the forward-premium cost it was absorbing.

The early closure does not end every funding channel. Separate facilities for state-owned companies and banks remain open through December, and the concessional swap for offshore borrowing offers a fixed annual rate of 1.5% for an average maturity of at least three years. Indian financial institutions have already sold a record $8 billion of dollar bonds this year, exceeding the previous full-year high of $7.92 billion in 2019. ICICI Bank was marketing another transaction Monday, and Kotak Mahindra Bank and Yes Bank had appointed advisers for potential benchmark sales. Banks may accelerate issuance before the deposit-related impetus fades, then slow once ordinary hedging costs again make offshore borrowing less economical.

India's sequence shows how a central-bank balance-sheet decision can redistribute rather than eliminate funding pressure. The deposit window had supported reserves, the rupee and domestic liquidity; ending it early raised local yields and reduced the expected currency benefit. The still-open borrowing facility encourages banks to issue dollar debt, shifting some demand toward global credit. Strong order books have allowed recent bank deals to price tighter than initial guidance, so the channel is functioning. Its marginal cost has moved from the RBI's future forward exposure toward domestic bondholders and offshore investors.

Greece offered the opposite sovereign signal by using fiscal overperformance to retire debt. The government plans about EUR13 billion of early repayments in 2026, including roughly EUR2.5 billion of European Financial Stability Mechanism loans and a EUR2.2 billion bond due in 2027. It also expects to reduce Treasury bills outstanding by EUR1.2 billion by December 31. The plan is not final, but it follows EUR6.9 billion of bailout-loan repayment in June and is intended to bring Greece's debt stock below Italy's by year-end.

The improvement rests on budget surpluses and liquidity rather than a maturity exchange alone. Greece expects its primary surplus to exceed target again, its debt-to-GDP ratio to fall to 137% this year from a prior 138.2% forecast, and cash reserves to exceed EUR30 billion at year-end. Early repayment lowers future financing needs, allowing the 2027 funding strategy to resemble this year's even after retiring the 2027 bond. Greece's 10-year yield has moved below those of Italy, France and the United Kingdom, illustrating how a credible reduction in supply can offset the global rise in term compensation.

Emerging-market inflation-linked debt reveals another form of differentiation. The $886 billion sector returned 11.1% in 2026 through Friday, against 1.6% for broader local debt and a 0.2% loss for the global aggregate benchmark. Currency appreciation amplified the result, particularly in Latin America, where the Colombian peso, Brazilian real and Mexican peso were the year's three strongest emerging-market currencies. Yet the trade is becoming more selective as implied inflation becomes expensive in Brazil and nominal long rates reach the mid-teens. Poland looks relatively cheap partly because heavier issuance lacks the natural pension-fund demand present in Brazil, while Chile and Colombia offer a more balanced inflation-linked valuation.

That dispersion matters because the common inflation shock is being filtered through different buyer bases and policy reactions. Turkey raised its year-end inflation projection to 28% from 26%; recent inflation readings also exceeded expectations in Argentina, India, South Africa and Romania, while Brazil and Colombia remained sticky. El Nino could add food and electricity pressure in Latin America. Linkers remain a useful expression of realized inflation and currency strength, but their prior return no longer substitutes for country-specific assessment of supply, real yield and central-bank credibility.

## Credit Access Masks Sharper Loss Allocation

Primary credit on Monday showed abundant cash coexisting with stricter discrimination. Blackstone Private Credit Fund sold $750 million of five-year notes after initially targeting roughly $500 million, supported by about $2 billion of peak orders. Blue Owl Technology Finance increased a June transaction by $400 million, twice its minimum target, after receiving about $1.05 billion of demand. Blue Owl's new debt priced at a 250-basis-point spread over Treasuries, inside the 265-basis-point premium on the existing bonds, and Blackstone priced at 205 basis points, about 25 basis points tighter than initial discussion.

Those results are notable because software exposure and redemption limits at some private-credit vehicles had raised concern earlier in the year. Second-quarter results reduced part of that anxiety, and the transactions demonstrated access at investment-grade terms. They did not reverse the broader selectivity seen when investors withdrew 36% of initial orders on average during the prior week after final spreads tightened. Strong books still depend on compensation surviving the syndication process.

Project Odyssey makes that price sensitivity explicit. Blackstone-backed QTS may increase the Microsoft-linked Georgia data-center financing to $3.9 billion after demand exceeded $8 billion. The five-year bonds are expected to be investment grade, yet a high-6% coupon and discounted issue price would produce a yield in the low-to-mid 7% area, comparable with single-B debt. Long-term leases and the Microsoft connection support the structure, but investors are still being paid for project, construction and concentration risks that do not sit directly on the hyperscaler's ordinary balance sheet. An April QTS transaction raised $4.6 billion for Microsoft compute capacity and attracted $12.5 billion of peak demand; the new yield shows that repeated access is not the same as cheap access.

Secondary credit supplied a more severe governance signal. Sammons Financial's June 2036 bonds widened to about 200 basis points over the benchmark from 147 basis points a week earlier, their weakest level since issuance. A report focused on links between the insurer and Guggenheim Partners, including filings that described Sammons as a related party and acknowledged incentives that could create conflicts. Hunterbrook Media disclosed that its investment affiliate was short the bonds, an important qualification to the report's incentives. Fitch had rated Sammons A- in June, citing very strong capital alongside modestly elevated risk-asset exposure.

The concern extends beyond one spread move. Sammons had been Guggenheim's largest shareholder, and Guggenheim managed tens of billions of dollars for the insurer. U.S. prosecutors and regulators are examining loans from insurers connected to Mark Walter that were directed toward other parts of his business empire. Guggenheim's first-lien term loan due November 2031 was quoted below 80 cents on Monday, down from around par on July 20. The combination of related-party exposure, cross-ownership and declining debt prices makes control and asset-transfer risk more important than the benign aggregate high-grade calendar.

Brazil showed how restrictive rates and fiscal uncertainty can turn macro restraint into corporate distress. The central bank's activity index fell 0.64% in June, worse than the 0.5% consensus decline and the largest drop since May 2025. The economy still expanded 0.2% in the second quarter and 2.35% from a year earlier, but rate-sensitive sectors are losing momentum after the first quarter's fiscal boost. Policymakers cut the Selic rate by 25 basis points for a fourth consecutive meeting in August to 14%, leaving September dependent on incoming inflation and activity. Inflation remains above the 3% target, limiting the speed of relief.

Finance Minister Dario Durigan acknowledged that investor concern about mandatory spending and the public-debt trajectory is justified. The real had weakened in five consecutive sessions the prior week, and foreign investors withdrew more than 13.5 billion reais, or $2.6 billion, from local equities through August 12 as President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva strengthened his election lead. Inflation expectations remain above target through 2028. Durigan identified fiscal policy as the main government-controlled lever for reducing structurally high rates, yet he did not endorse changes to pension indexation or the fiscal framework's spending rules. Recognition of the problem has not yet produced a specific adjustment.

Casas Bahia illustrates the corporate consequence. The retailer entered court-supervised bankruptcy protection after its 2024 out-of-court restructuring failed to restore liquidity. It cited high interest rates, tighter credit, financing costs, weak consumption and working-capital pressure, and listed 17.3 billion reais of liabilities. First-half net revenue was 14.4 billion reais, while the net loss reached 11.2 billion reais, 18.4% wider than a year earlier. The company closed 298 stores and plans to keep its remaining operations open while extending debt maturities. An available legal process can preserve operations, but it does not restore earnings visibility or creditor value.

Braskem remains a separate deadline-driven restructuring. Petrobras is considering longer payment periods, lower interest rates and increased naphtha supply after tighter prior terms reduced its share of Braskem's feedstock to about 30% from as much as 70%, forcing the petrochemical company to borrow more from banks. Better commercial terms could reduce working-capital borrowing and leverage. No decision or timing has been set, however, and Braskem must secure support from holders of at least one-third of its debt by August 24 to complete an out-of-court solution and avoid judicial recovery.

The proposed support also exposes stakeholder conflict. Braskem shares had secured 21 billion reais of unpaid bank loans that were ultimately sold to a fund managed by IG4 Capital, which now shares control. Bondholders including Elliott Investment Management and Contrarian Capital want Petrobras to provide equity, working capital or junior debt. Petrobras has resisted an equity injection because a larger ownership stake could require consolidation of Braskem's debt onto its own balance sheet. Commercial concessions may improve liquidity without resolving how losses and new capital are divided among the state-controlled shareholder, banks and bondholders.

Modernland Realty shows a similar transfer of value in Asia. The Indonesian developer proposes extending its $274.5 million dollar bond from April 2027 to June 2028 and eventually exchanging it for perpetual securities backed by assets transferred to a creditor-controlled vehicle. Holders would receive $50 per $1,000 of principal upfront, accrue 3% payment-in-kind interest, and capitalize unpaid interest into principal. Part of the current collateral would be released to secure a new $34 million facility. The August 24 voting deadline makes the package a current decision point: maturity relief and new liquidity arrive in exchange for delayed cash interest, altered security and a longer recovery horizon.

## Forward Market Significance

The July FOMC minutes on August 19 and Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks later in the month need to resolve how much weight policymakers place on the recent sequence of softer employment, inflation and retail-sales data. The July decision was 9-3 to hold rates, and current pricing has moved the next increase to January. Language suggesting the hold was closer than that vote implies, or emphasizing that more than 55% of core goods prices are still rising, could pull the 2-year yield back toward the long-end selloff. A patient interpretation that requires several more data points before tightening would preserve the steep curve and leave fiscal supply, AI issuance and real yields as the dominant constraints on duration.

The $16 billion 20-year Treasury auction is the next direct clearing-price test for the maturity sector that weakened most. The 30-year closed at 5.31%, 6 basis points higher on the day, as cash trading beyond 20 years rose 15.1% from the prior session to $134.4 billion in original-face value. A result close to the prevailing when-issued level with stable secondary trading would show that demand remains available after the latest concession. A material tail or renewed post-auction steepening would indicate that record August corporate supply and the global rise in sovereign yields are still overwhelming the relief from a less hawkish Fed path.

The energy channel requires a physical resolution rather than another diplomatic headline. Continued covert crude transfers, restored vessel passage and lower freight or insurance costs would reduce the pressure that lifted Brent to $91.12 and keep the latest Treasury selloff centered in real yields. A failure of alternative flows, renewed attacks or tighter enforcement around Iranian ports would broaden the shock into inflation compensation and policy pricing. The distinction will be visible in whether breakevens and the 2-year yield begin rising with oil, or whether the curve continues to steepen with most of the adjustment in long real rates.
